options.title: How Do You Dig a Railway Under London?
options.first_line: To dig the Elizabeth line under London, Crossrail sent in machines {fact1} metres long. So how does one work?
options.first_frame: A long glowing tunnel boring machine shown in cutaway under London's streets, its cutterhead already spinning into the clay.

options.title: Inside the {fact1}-Metre Machine Under London
options.first_line: This machine is {fact1} metres long, and it dug the Elizabeth line under London. How?
options.first_frame: Close on the spinning steel cutterhead biting into lit clay, then the camera pulls back along the machine's whole length.

options.title: How Did Crossrail Tunnel Past the Tube?
options.first_line: Crossrail dug a brand new railway under London, right through a city already full of Tube tunnels. How?
options.first_frame: London's ground sliced open: old Tube tunnels glowing in the clay, and a tunnel machine's cutterhead spinning toward them.

why: It names something people ride (the Tube) and poses a real how-is-that-possible puzzle (a new railway threaded through a city already full of tunnels) without giving the answer, while A and B lean on a machine length that is only big and the first frame of C shows the whole problem on mute.
